title: Grateful Dead Live at Student Center on 1969-03-28

ai_review.summary: A pristine sound‑board capture of a classic ’69 show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star, The Eleven and an epic That's It For The Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is lauded as crystal‑clear for its era—thanks to Miller’s meticulous cleaning—and delivers the raw power of a spring‑1969 set. Fans repeatedly point out Jerry Garcia’s incendiary guitar work on Dark Star, the thunderous Eleven, and a standout Death Don't Have No Mercy, while Phil Lesh’s bass shines through the improvisations. Overall the performance is celebrated as an essential example of the Dead at their exploratory peak.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (15 × 5‑star, 2 × 4‑star) praise both the musical performance and the high‑fidelity soundboard source; only one brief negative comment does not shift the overall assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as superb, crisp, and clean for a 1969 tape; Miller’s cleanup work is credited with delivering great fidelity and minimal noise.

standout_songs: That's It For The Other One (Cryptical Reprise)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A classic spring‑'69 set with a tight first half and an explosive second set featuring Dark Star, the Eleven, and the TIFTOO suite; pacing is energetic yet retains the improvisational ebb and flow fans love.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for blistering solos, new licks, and a "zone" performance on Dark Star; his guitar work is described as intense, buzzing like an angry hornet.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a strong, audible bass line during The Eleven and overall solid support throughout the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned stepping up when Jerry drops out, contributing to jams in later parts of The Eleven and other segments.
band_member_comments.Drums: One humorous note about a 17‑second drum track being split; no substantive performance critique.
